baseHeader.methodology: Source-linked original summaries and reference-guided educational reconstructions. Models and motion are unvalidated; artist titles do not independently verify taxonomy. Navigation groups are not a universal kingdom system. Microbial behavior depends on strain and conditions. Expansion entries are individually referenced authored morphology studies; legacy Protista/Monera reporting categories do not replace modern domains. Actual screenshots, software checks and draft status are distinct from independent scientific validation.

before.range: See species accounts for distribution; recorded occurrences below are not native-range boundaries.
before.summary: Two elongated dark valves enclose a bivalve body. Byssal threads attach many adults to a substrate.

anatomy.name: Valves
anatomy.description: Elongated inequilateral valves with concentric growth cues and no radial ribs; a selected variable shell form, not a Mytilus-complex diagnosis.

anatomy.name: Hinge
anatomy.description: Upper valve opens about the retained dorsal hinge line. Adductor, ligament mechanics and exhalant flow are absent.

anatomy.name: Byssus
anatomy.description: Curved byssal thread cues retain their substrate anchors during valve gape; no adhesion forces or thread mechanics.

behaviors.label: Filtration — pending
behaviors.description: Filtration is not implemented. Separate partial valve gape moves the same upper valve about its hinge while lower valve and byssal anchors remain fixed; no filtering particles, flow or measured environmental response.
behaviors.evidence: Qualitative morphology and behavior context; no measured kinematics or physiology

rendering.reason: Feeding, radular contact, particle capture and fluid/physiological mechanisms are not implemented.

visual.fidelity: Species-specific authored reference reconstruction; partly stylized and unmeasured
visual.description: Tapered inequilateral blue-black valves, original growth-line relief and variable sheen, persistent byssal threads and hinge-only upper-valve gape. Shell asymmetry, umbo/ligament, margin fit, erosion and internal soft anatomy remain simplified; the selected photo includes prepared cut/open shells and does not demonstrate live feeding. Original authored reconstruction, partly stylized and unmeasured; no independent biological validation.
